arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Berreth argued Section 1446(a) requires a short and plain statement of grounds.
Mr. Sharp argued Section 1447(d) bars Supreme Court review of the remand order.
Justice Roberts asked why dissenters did not explain their reasoning if the Tenth Circuit relied on different grounds.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the standard for removing a lawsuit from state to federal court. the sides that brought the case argue the law requires only a statement of grounds. the opposing sides argue the court needed proof to verify jurisdiction.

paragraphs: This dispute defines the burden of proof for removing cases to federal court. It affects how quickly parties can access federal tribunals. It shapes the initial procedural steps in federal litigation.
